epic_title: The calendar view: grid, navigation, indicators, interaction
summary: This epic owns everything the user sees and clicks inside the calendar view itself: the month grid (including adjacent-month days and the week-number column), moving between months and back to today, the click/modifier-click/hover/right-click behaviour of every cell type (day, week number, month header), the indicator dots on a cell and the detail shown for them, and keeping all of that current as files, settings, the active note, and the clock change. It boundaries against NOTE (which owns actually opening or creating a note file), CMD (which owns the command/ribbon that opens this view), SET (which owns the settings values themselves, not the view's reaction to them) and FMT (which owns the week-number value, not its display column).

stories.title: Render the month grid with adjacent-month days and the week-number column
stories.story: As someone scanning a month at a glance, I want the grid to always show a full 6-week rectangle with the surrounding days filled in and clearly marked as not-this-month, so that the layout never jumps in height and I can still see the start/end of neighbouring weeks.
stories.rationale: A stable, complete grid is the foundation every other interaction in this epic is drawn on top of.

acceptance_criteria.given: any month is displayed
then: the grid always shows exactly 6 rows of 7 days, regardless of how many days the month has
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts > AC-CAL-01.1: the grid is a full 6x7 rectangle > returns 6 rows of 7 days for 24 consecutive months and every week start / > covers 42 consecutive days with no gap or repeat / > still returns 6 rows for a 28-day February that starts on the week start. Evidence is on the grid data model, not the rendered table -- renderGrid (calendar.ts:142-197) is two unconditional loops over that data, which is code review rather than measurement.

acceptance_criteria.given: the displayed month does not start on the grid's first weekday column
then: the leading empty cells are filled with the trailing days of the previous month
those leading cells are visually distinguished from the current month's days
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts > AC-CAL-01.2 / AC-CAL-01.3: adjacent-month days fill the rectangle > fills the leading cells with the trailing days of the previous month / > marks exactly the displayed month own days as not adjacent, in order. The visual distinction itself is a CSS opacity rule on the isAdjacentMonth flag, confirmed by code review.

acceptance_criteria.given: the displayed month's last day falls before the end of the grid's last row
then: the trailing empty cells are filled with the leading days of the next month
those trailing cells are visually distinguished from the current month's days
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts > AC-CAL-01.2 / AC-CAL-01.3: adjacent-month days fill the rectangle > fills the trailing cells with the leading days of the next month / > marks exactly the displayed month own days as not adjacent, in order.

acceptance_criteria.given: the week-number column is enabled
then: each week row shows a week-number cell at the start of the row
every displayed week number agrees with the week number shown elsewhere for the same date and the same settings
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts > AC-CAL-01.4: one anchor for the number, the dot and the click > row anchor matches the displayed number for weekStart=0..6 (14 cases across 2026-12-15 and 2027-01-15) / > numbers a Sunday-start row by its own week, not the previous one; > AC-CAL-01.4: the week number agrees with the weekly note name > matches the weekly note path of every row across the year boundary / > follows the locale week when the weekly note format uses ww / > ... uses WW; > AC-CAL-01.4: nested-only weekly formats > numbers every row to match the note path a nested-only format writes; plus src/ui/calendarDots.test.ts > DotScanner.getWeekNotePaths > scans exactly the rows the grid draws, one anchor per row / > finds the note of a Sunday-start row under the row own week. This criterion drove the real defect this ticket fixed: the displayed number and the note actually opened disagreed for any non-Monday week start.

acceptance_criteria.given: the week-number column is disabled
then: no week-number column or cells are shown
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts > "AC-CAL-01.5: ..." renders the grid twice, with showWeekNumbers on and off, and asserts both states: on, one .calendaric-weeknum-header, six .calendaric-weeknum-cell, and eight cells per row; off, zero of each and seven cells per row. Mutation-checked by the orchestrator at BOTH branches of the setting, separately: forcing the header cell at calendar.ts:101 fails it, and forcing the row cells at calendar.ts:141 fails it. This supersedes the earlier evidence, which reported the criterion UNSETTLED because the repository had no DOM harness -- happy-dom now runs per file via a `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` pragma, and src/__mocks__/obsidianDom.ts shims createEl, createDiv, empty and addClass, which is exactly the set src/ui/ calls.

acceptance_criteria.given: the displayed month spans a leap-year February or a December-to-January year boundary
then: adjacent-month days on the grid carry the correct date and year across the boundary
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarUtils.test.ts > AC-CAL-01.6: dates stay correct across leap years and year boundaries > keeps 29 February inside a leap-year grid / > produces no 29 February in a non-leap year / > carries the next year on December trailing days / > carries the previous year on January leading days.

stories.title: Navigate between months and return to today
stories.story: As someone planning ahead or looking back, I want to step the grid forward and backward one month at a time and jump straight back to the current month, so that I can browse freely without losing track of where 'now' is.
stories.rationale: Browsing is the most frequent interaction with the view, and it must never require creating or opening any note to use.

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is showing any month
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates the 'next month' control
then: the grid shows the following month
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarNav.test.ts > "AC-CAL-02.1: shows the following month", plus a step out of a 31-day month into a shorter one and a second step from a month already visited. The displayed date is held on the first of the month, so repeated steps cannot drift the way a 31st does when moment clamps it into February. Mutation-checked by the orchestrator: stepping by a week instead of a month fails 7 of the 14 tests.

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is showing any month
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates the 'previous month' control
then: the grid shows the preceding month
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarNav.test.ts > "AC-CAL-02.2: shows the preceding month", plus January stepping back into December of the previous year.

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is showing a month other than the current one
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates the dedicated 'return to today' control
then: the grid shows the current month
today's cell is visible in that month
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarNav.test.ts > "AC-CAL-02.3: shows the current month again from far away in either direction" and "AC-CAL-02.3: leaves today's cell in the grid it returns to". The second reads the real clock, because getMonthGrid derives isToday from window.moment(), and asserts the returned grid holds exactly one isToday cell rather than one borrowed from an adjacent month.

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is already showing the current month
acceptance_criteria.when: the view renders the 'return to today' control
then: the control is shown in an inactive state
activating it while inactive has no effect
acceptance_criteria.evidence: HALF SETTLED, and the missing half needs a DOM harness this repository does not have. The second clause is proved: vitest: src/ui/calendarNav.test.ts > "AC-CAL-02.4: reports the inactive state and does nothing when activated" asserts atCurrentMonth is true, that clicking leaves the month unchanged, and that the redraw counter stays at zero, so the handler really is inert; three further tests cover repeated clicks, the return to the active state after leaving the month, and September 2027 not matching September 2026. Mutation-checked by the orchestrator: removing the early exit from toToday fails 2 tests. The FIRST clause -- that the control is SHOWN in an inactive state -- is not proved. calendar.ts sets is-disabled and aria-disabled from nav.atCurrentMonth, but nothing tests that link: vitest runs in the node environment, neither jsdom nor happy-dom is installed, and calendar.ts relies on Obsidian own DOM extensions (createEl, createDiv, empty, addClass). This is the same missing harness that holds AC-CAL-01.5 and the "user sees the notice" clause of US-ARCH-04 open.

acceptance_criteria.given: the grid is showing December of any year
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates the 'next month' control
then: the grid shows January of the following year
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/calendarNav.test.ts > "AC-CAL-02.5: shows January of the following year", plus the same crossing from a December reached by stepping rather than by construction.

decisions.title: The plugin ships in English only
decisions.decision: All user-facing text is English. No localisation layer, no translated labels, no locale-dependent strings. Controls that the previous component library labelled with a translated word use an icon with an English tooltip instead.
decisions.rationale: Stated by the owner. It removes a whole class of open question about which surfaces need translating, and keeps narrow controls readable in a sidebar. Note this is about interface text only: date and weekday names still follow the configured locale, because those come from the date formatter, not from the plugin's own copy.

stories.title: Click a day cell to open or create its note
stories.story: As someone keeping a daily journal, I want clicking any day in the grid to take me to that day's note, offering to create it if it does not exist yet, so that the grid is a single place to reach any day.
stories.rationale: This is the single most common way a periodic note gets opened from the calendar.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell already has a note
then: the existing note opens in the active pane
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, the AC-CAL-03.1 cases -- an existing note is opened through the workspace port in the active-pane mode, and nothing is written to the vault. The criterion is testable_by manual, so the on-screen result is not observed here; what is proven is the decision this plugin makes and the call it hands to the port.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell has no note yet and creating without confirmation is configured
then: the note is created and opens in the active pane, with no confirmation step
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, the AC-CAL-03.2 cases (nine of them) -- a missing note is created and then opened, with no confirmation step, and concurrent activations create exactly one note. That last part took three review rounds: the coordination first keyed on nothing, then on the adapter instance (which is per calendar pane), and now on the underlying vault. The criterion is testable_by manual, so the on-screen result is not observed here; what is proven is the decision this plugin makes and the call it hands to the port.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell has no note yet and confirming before creation is configured
then: a confirmation dialog appears naming the day before any file is created
accepting the dialog creates the note and opens it in the active pane
dismissing the dialog creates nothing and leaves the grid unchanged
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, the AC-CAL-03.3 cases -- the confirmation is requested BEFORE anything is written (asserted by checking the file does not exist at the moment of asking), and dismissing it creates nothing. The criterion is testable_by manual, so the on-screen result is not observed here; what is proven is the decision this plugin makes and the call it hands to the port.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell (with or without a note)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks it while holding the split-pane modifier key
then: the note opens in a new split instead of the active pane, being created first if it did not already exist
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, the AC-CAL-03.4 cases (six) -- the split destination is chosen on the platform-correct modifier, asserted separately for macOS and non-macOS after a first implementation treated Ctrl and Meta as equivalent everywhere, and the note is created first when missing. The criterion is testable_by manual, so the on-screen result is not observed here; what is proven is the decision this plugin makes and the call it hands to the port.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell already has a note
acceptance_criteria.when: the user hovers it while holding the preview modifier key
then: the correct native preview of that note's content appears near the cell
the grid does not navigate or open the note
acceptance_criteria.evidence: UNSETTLED, reported rather than judged: the criterion asks that the correct NATIVE preview of the note content appears near the cell. This plugin only emits the hover-link event and registers the source; the preview itself is rendered by Obsidian Page Preview plugin, honouring its own per-source modifier setting. Tests cover the payload and the modifier gate (src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, AC-CAL-03.5 cases), which is our whole half -- but whether a correct preview appears cannot be claimed from here and needs a live host.

acceptance_criteria.given: the clicked day cell belongs to the leading or trailing (adjacent-month) part of the grid
then: the same open-or-create behaviour applies as for a day in the displayed month
the grid keeps showing the same month it showed before the click
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest: src/ui/cellActions.test.ts, the AC-CAL-03.6 cases -- a day from an adjacent month resolves to its own date and gets the same open-or-create treatment, and the click does not mutate the cell Moment. The criterion is testable_by manual, so the on-screen result is not observed here; what is proven is the decision this plugin makes and the call it hands to the port. The clause that the grid keeps showing the same month is structural: no month state reaches openOrCreateNote at all.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day cell has no note yet
acceptance_criteria.when: the user hovers it while holding the preview modifier key
then: a preview is shown stating that the note does not exist yet
no file is created by hovering
acceptance_criteria.evidence: UNSETTLED, reported rather than judged: same boundary as AC-CAL-03.5. The test asserts the linktext handed over for a missing note and that nothing is written to the vault, but the "note does not exist yet" text comes from Obsidian, not from this plugin, so its appearance is unverified without a live host.

decisions.title: Every gesture on a week-number cell resolves the same date
decisions.decision: Click, hover and right-click on a week-number cell all resolve to the same reference date for that week, whatever the configured week-start day.
decisions.rationale: The old behaviour could resolve a different date for click than for hover, so the preview showed one note and the click opened another. That is a defect, not a feature worth preserving.

stories.title: Open the month's note from the header, and reset to today from a separate control
stories.story: As someone who keeps a monthly note, I want clicking the month header to take me to that month's note, and a separate, dedicated control to jump back to today, so that neither action is at risk of accidentally triggering the other.
stories.rationale: This carries forward a feature the user relies on today that is currently implemented in a fragile, easily-broken way; the rewrite must make it a real, first-class part of the header rather than a workaround layered on top of it.

acceptance_criteria.given: monthly periodic notes are configured and available
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the month header
then: the displayed month's note opens in the active pane, being created first if it did not already exist
the displayed month on the grid does not change because of this click
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.1: opens the displayed month's note in the active pane, leaving the grid where it was", "AC-CAL-05.1: creates the displayed month's note first when it is missing, then opens it"; src/ui/cellActions.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.1: asks for a monthly note by its month, then creates and opens it". Proven red by mutate-check: replacing the header's open with nav.toToday() fails 5 of the 9 render tests.

acceptance_criteria.given: monthly periodic notes are configured and available
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the month header while holding the split-pane modifier key
then: the note opens in a new split instead of the active pane, being created first if it did not already exist
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.2: opens the month's note in a split when the click carries the split modifier", "AC-CAL-05.2: creates the missing month note first, then opens it in the split". Proven red by mutate-check: dropping the click event on the way to openOrCreateNote fails both split tests and no others.

acceptance_criteria.given: monthly periodic notes are not configured or not available

then: the grid resets its displayed month to today, matching the behaviour of the dedicated 'return to today' control
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.3: resets the grid to the current month when monthly notes are not configured". Proven red by mutate-check: forcing the settings.month.enabled guard false fails this test alone.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note already exists for the displayed month
acceptance_criteria.when: the user right-clicks the month header
then: that note's file context menu appears at the click position
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.4: right-clicking a month that has a note opens that file's context menu at the click", "AC-CAL-05.4: right-clicking a month with no note opens no file menu". Proven red by mutate-check: deleting menu.showAtMouseEvent(event) fails the first, deleting the missing-file guard fails the second.

acceptance_criteria.given: the view is assembled
then: it exposes its own dedicated, addressable click target for 'open this month's note'
that target is not identified by matching incidental markup or styling produced by an unrelated UI component
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.test.ts "AC-CAL-05.5: the header's click target is its own element, not the month/year markup or a nav control". Proven red by mutate-check: removing the calendaric-month-header class fails 8 of 9 render tests, and leaving the title's display spans in place across a re-render fails this test.

decisions.title: The month header reacts to a configuration change immediately
decisions.decision: When monthly notes stop being available while the calendar is open, the next click on the month header already behaves as the fallback. No reopening of the view is required, in either direction.
decisions.rationale: The grid is already required to redraw as soon as settings are saved. A header that lags behind the grid it sits on would be inconsistent with the reactivity the same epic demands everywhere else.

stories.title: Right-click a day or week cell for file actions
stories.story: As someone managing my notes from the calendar, I want to right-click a day or week that already has a note to get its usual file actions, so that I do not have to locate the file elsewhere to rename or delete it.
stories.rationale: The context menu is the calendar's entry point into standard file management, including whatever other installed plugins add to it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day or week cell already has a note
then: that note's file context menu appears at the click position

acceptance_criteria.given: a day or week cell has no note
then: no context menu appears

acceptance_criteria.when: the menu opens from a day or week cell
then: those contributed items also appear in the menu

acceptance_criteria.given: the file context menu is open
then: the underlying note file is removed

stories.title: Show indicator dots for note existence and amount of content
stories.story: As someone scanning the month for how much I've written, I want each day and week to show a small dot when a note exists, filled in proportion to how much is in it, so that I can spot thin or empty periods at a glance without opening anything.
stories.rationale: This is the one indicator the vault actually uses today, and the extension point behind it must stay open to other indicators later.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day, week, or month has no note
then: no indicator dot is shown for it
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.dots.test.ts "AC-CAL-07.1: a day or week with no note shows no dot of either kind"; red when a day cell draws its dot without a note (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: a note exists and has at least one word in it
then: an indicator dot is shown with at least one segment filled
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.dots.test.ts "AC-CAL-07.2: a note with words shows a word-count dot with a segment filled, on day and week cells"; red when the word dot loses its class (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: the word-count threshold in effect for the cell is 250 (the default, or an explicit setting of 250)
then: a note of 1, 249, 250, or 499 words fills exactly one dot segment
a note of 500 words fills exactly two dot segments

acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarDots.test.ts "AC-CAL-07.3: at a threshold of 250, fills one segment per 250 words, at least one, at most five" and "... a threshold that is not a positive whole number falls back to 250"; red under floor->ceil and under a weakened threshold guard (mutations). The threshold is a parameter defaulting to 250; no setting carries it yet

acceptance_criteria.given: a cell has data for both built-in indicator sources that ship in this release: note existence and word count
then: the note-exists dot and the word-count dot both appear on the cell

acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.dots.test.ts "AC-CAL-07.4: a note with words shows both dots, told apart by class and colour" incl. the is-active cells; red when the word dot takes the exists class (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: one of the two built-in dots (note-exists or word-count) has nothing to show for a given cell (for example, no note exists yet)
then: that dot does not appear for that cell, while the other built-in dot is unaffected
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.dots.test.ts "AC-CAL-07.5: an empty note keeps its note-exists dot and shows no word-count dot"; red when a zero-segment word dot is drawn (mutation)

decisions.title: Words per dot is a global setting with a default of 250
decisions.decision: Calendaric keeps the word-count threshold that decides how many dots a day shows. It is one global number, default 250, editable in settings. A value that is not a positive whole number falls back to the default and the settings field says so. The Calendar import carries the existing wordsPerDot value across.
decisions.rationale: US-CAL-07 requires configured word-count thresholds while SET named no control and no default, and MIG dropped the existing value on the claim that Calendaric has no equivalent field. An implementation could satisfy every criterion and still leave the user no way to configure the behaviour CAL promises. This vault's Calendar plugin has wordsPerDot 250, so the default matches what the user already sees.

stories.title: See indicator detail without needing to hover
stories.story: As someone using the calendar on a keyboard or a touchscreen laptop, I want to see the full detail behind a cell's indicators without needing to hover, so that I get the same information a mouse user gets from hovering.
stories.rationale: A dot alone only shows a rough level; the detail view is what makes it actionable, and it must be reachable without a pointer, from a keyboard or a touchscreen laptop.

then: a detail view appears near the cell listing each indicator's value

acceptance_criteria.when: the pointer leaves that cell and does not move onto the detail view itself
then: the detail view closes within the 250 ms dismissal delay

acceptance_criteria.given: a cell has one or more indicators, on a touchscreen laptop
then: the same detail information hover shows is displayed
no hover gesture is required to see it

acceptance_criteria.given: a cell has no indicator data at all
acceptance_criteria.when: it is hovered, given keyboard focus, or tapped
then: no detail view appears

acceptance_criteria.given: a cell has one or more indicators
acceptance_criteria.when: the user moves keyboard focus to that cell

decisions.title: The first release is desktop only, and says so in the manifest
decisions.decision: manifest.json declares isDesktopOnly true, which means Obsidian will not install Calendaric on a phone or tablet. No story may promise phone behaviour while that stands. Hover-dependent surfaces still need a pointer-free path, because a desktop user can be on a keyboard or a touchscreen laptop, but that is an accessibility requirement, not a mobile one. Mobile support is an icebox entry, gated on replacing the desktop-only call behind DEC-03's adapter.
decisions.rationale: DEC-03 already declared desktop only, and US-CAL-08 was written for a laptop and a phone. Both cannot hold: isDesktopOnly true blocks installation on mobile outright, so a phone criterion could never be run, let alone passed. Desktop first without closing the door is the stated position, and one adapter plus an icebox entry is what keeps the door open.

stories.title: Keep the grid's cells and dots in sync with the vault and its settings
stories.story: As someone editing notes from outside the calendar, I want the grid to update itself when a note appears, disappears, is renamed, or a relevant setting changes, so that what I see never goes stale while the view is open.
stories.rationale: The grid is read constantly but the notes behind it are created and edited elsewhere; staleness would make it actively misleading.

acceptance_criteria.given: a note matching a day or week format is created outside the view (another pane, sync, or externally)
acceptance_criteria.when: the file lands in the vault while the view is open
then: the corresponding cell's indicator appears without the user reloading or interacting with the view
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.liveRefresh.test.ts "AC-CAL-09.1: a day or week note created elsewhere gains its cell's dot with no interaction"; red when create/delete/rename stop triggering a redraw (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: a note matching a day or week format is deleted
acceptance_criteria.when: the deletion happens while the view is open
then: the corresponding cell's indicator disappears without the user reloading or interacting with the view
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.liveRefresh.test.ts "AC-CAL-09.2: a day or week note deleted elsewhere loses its cell's dot with no interaction"; red under the same mutation

acceptance_criteria.given: a note matching a day or week format is renamed
acceptance_criteria.when: the rename happens while the view is open
then: the cell for the old name loses its indicator
the cell for the new name gains an indicator, if the new name still matches a recognised date
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.liveRefresh.test.ts "AC-CAL-09.3: a rename moves the dot from the old date's cell to the new one", the week-row case and "... a rename to a name that matches no date removes the dot and adds none"; red under the same mutation

acceptance_criteria.given: a setting that affects the calendar's own display changes (for example, an indicator threshold or the week-number column)
then: the grid re-renders immediately to reflect the new setting
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.liveRefresh.test.ts "AC-CAL-09.4: a saved display setting re-renders the grid at once" (CalendarWidget.refreshSettings, which main.ts onSettingsChange reaches through CalendarView.refresh); red when refreshSettings stops re-rendering (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: the periodic-notes configuration (folders, formats, or which granularities are enabled) changes elsewhere
then: the grid re-indexes existing notes and re-renders to reflect the new configuration
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.liveRefresh.test.ts "AC-CAL-09.5: a changed format or folder re-scans the notes and redraws the dots" and "... a granularity switched off drops its dots"; red under the same mutation

stories.title: Highlight and reveal the currently active note
stories.story: As someone editing a periodic note in another pane, I want the calendar to show me which cell that note belongs to, and to be able to jump the view to it, so that I always know where I am in the calendar without hunting for it.
stories.rationale: The highlight is the calendar's answer to 'where am I', and it must track the active pane, not just clicks made inside the view itself.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day or week note becomes the active file in any pane
acceptance_criteria.when: it is visible in the currently displayed month
then: its cell is visibly highlighted as the active note
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest src/ui/calendarRender.activeNote.test.ts 'AC-CAL-10.1' at 9215b2e: day and week cells get is-active from file-open in any pane, matched by resolveFileDate identity; mutation (day/week compare forced false) turns it red

acceptance_criteria.given: a cell is highlighted as the active note
acceptance_criteria.when: a file that is not a day or week note becomes active
then: the previous highlight is cleared
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest 'AC-CAL-10.2' at 9215b2e: a non-periodic file or an empty pane clears is-active; mutation (keep previous path on null file) turns it red

acceptance_criteria.given: the active file is a day or week note whose date falls outside the currently displayed month, and the view is asked to reveal the active note
then: the view navigates to the month containing that note
the note's cell is highlighted
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest 'AC-CAL-10.3' at 9215b2e: revealActiveNote navigates via MonthNavigation.show to the note's month and highlights; month notes are ignored; mutations (never navigate; accept any granularity) turn it red

acceptance_criteria.given: the active file is a day or week note already within the currently displayed month, and the view is asked to reveal the active note
then: the view highlights the note's cell without navigating away from the month already shown
acceptance_criteria.evidence: vitest 'AC-CAL-10.4' at 9215b2e: a note inside the shown month, including a week row reaching into it, highlights without navigating; mutation (navigate unless the row start is in the month) turns it red

stories.title: Keep 'today' current while the view stays open
stories.story: As someone who leaves the calendar open across midnight, I want today's cell to advance on its own, so that the view never quietly shows yesterday as today.
stories.rationale: The view has no reason to be reopened during normal use, so it must roll itself over rather than relying on the user to refresh it.

acceptance_criteria.given: the view is open and currently displaying today's month with today's cell marked as today
acceptance_criteria.when: midnight passes while the view stays open
then: the marked 'today' cell automatically advances to the new date, with no action from the user
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.today.test.ts "AC-CAL-11.1: a tick after midnight marks the new day as today" — drives CalendarWidget.refresh(), the call CalendarView's 60 s registerInterval makes; red when refresh() stops re-rendering (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: the view is open and currently displaying today's month, and midnight passes into a new month
then: the displayed month advances along with the marked 'today' cell
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.today.test.ts "AC-CAL-11.2: a tick after midnight into a new month shows the new month" plus the stepped-away-and-back, stepped-ahead and December-to-January cases; red when refresh() drops nav.followClock() (mutation)

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has navigated away to view a day or month other than today
then: the view does not automatically jump back to today
it stays showing whatever the user had navigated to
acceptance_criteria.evidence: src/ui/calendarRender.today.test.ts "AC-CAL-11.3: a tick into a new month leaves an earlier month on screen" plus the later-month and plain-day-rollover cases; red when followClock() follows the clock unconditionally (mutation)

stories.title: Position hover and menu overlays near their trigger
stories.story: As someone opening a popover or a suggestion list from the calendar, I want that overlay to stay fully visible and anchored to whatever triggered it, so that it is never clipped off the edge of the window or left floating in the wrong place.
stories.rationale: This is the shared positioning behaviour the indicator popover (and future overlay-driven features) depend on to be usable near the edges of the window.

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay is triggered near the edge of the window
then: it is positioned so it stays fully visible rather than being clipped by the window edge

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay is open and its trigger element moves or scrolls out from under it
then: the overlay's position updates to stay anchored to the trigger, or the overlay closes

acceptance_criteria.given: a list-type overlay (such as a suggestion list) is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user presses the arrow keys
then: keyboard focus moves between the overlay's items
the overlay stays open while doing so

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks or taps outside it
then: the overlay closes

acceptance_criteria.given: an overlay is open and its trigger element is removed from the page while the overlay is still showing (for example, the grid re-renders)
then: the overlay closes rather than being left anchored to nothing

decisions.title: One overlay-positioning mechanism, shared by every overlay
decisions.decision: The calendar's hover popover and the settings screen's autocomplete use the same positioning behaviour and the same implementation.
decisions.rationale: Two implementations of the same edge-avoidance and anchoring rules is exactly the duplication this rewrite exists to remove. It also means one place to fix when a popover is clipped.

stories.title: Show which period an open note belongs to
stories.story: As someone reading a note from three weeks ago, I want the note itself to tell me which day it is, so that I do not have to decode the filename to know where I am.
stories.rationale: This is on in the live vault and renders in every open periodic note today. An earlier icebox entry deferred it on the claim that it was unused; the claim was wrong.

acceptance_criteria.given: the feature is enabled and a note for a recognised period is open
then: a label in the note names the period in words, such as Today or Last week
the label follows the note's own date, not the current date

acceptance_criteria.given: the feature is enabled and a file that is not a periodic note is open
then: no label appears
the note's own content is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the feature is enabled and then disabled in settings
acceptance_criteria.when: a note for a recognised period is opened after the setting is disabled
then: no label appears in that note

acceptance_criteria.given: the note matched for the label is an inexact, prefix match rather than an exact filename match
then: the label includes a marker indicating an inexact match
a label for an exactly-matched note shows no such marker

acceptance_criteria.given: a note is already open, either showing or not showing the label
then: if the setting is now enabled, the label appears in that already-open note without the note being reopened
if the setting is now disabled, the label disappears from that already-open note without the note being reopened

acceptance_criteria.given: several notes are open in separate panes and one pane is closed
then: each remaining open periodic note still shows its own label
the closed pane leaves no label behind

notes: Moved out of ICE-04, which deferred this on evidence that only said no template or query references a timeline view. The feature does not need one: it mounts itself into every open markdown view.

Split per re-review finding 9: the day-strip navigation behaviour (stepping to a neighbouring day) is now its own story, US-CAL-14, because it is a distinct unit of value from showing the period label.

stories.title: Move to a neighbouring day from an open note's label
stories.story: As someone reading a note for any period, I want to step to a neighbouring day without leaving the note, so that I can move through the week from where I am.
stories.rationale: A label that only names the period is informative; the day strip is what makes it a way to move around.

acceptance_criteria.given: the label is shown on an open periodic note of any supported granularity — day, week, month or year
then: a strip of the seven days of that note's week appears
the week starts on the configured start-of-week day
the note's own day is marked when the note is a daily note, and today is marked when today falls in that week

acceptance_criteria.given: the day strip is open and a neighbouring day already has a note
then: the existing note for that day opens in the active pane
no new file is created for that day

acceptance_criteria.given: the day strip is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user activates a day that has no note
then: the note for that day is created and opens in the active pane
the configured template is applied

notes: Split from US-CAL-13 per re-review finding 9.
The strip offers days whatever the open note's granularity: the source renders it whenever the note resolves to a period at all, with no daily-only guard.

Almost every acceptance criterion in this epic is DOM/interaction-driven (click, hover, contextmenu, live vault events) and is only testable_by 'manual' or 'integration'. The exceptions are pure grid/date math and word-count-to-dot-fill logic (US-CAL-01, most of US-CAL-07), which are testable_by 'unit'.

US-CAL-03, US-CAL-04 and US-CAL-05 depend on NOTE's 'open or create a note for a date' capability and on FMT's/SET's resolution of where and how that note is named; this epic owns only the click/hover/menu request that triggers it and the resulting view-level effect (which pane, whether the grid navigates), never the file operation itself. Exact NOTE story IDs were not guessed and are left out of depends_on.

The conflict between 'open the month note' and 'reset to today' on the month header is resolved in US-CAL-05: the header always tries to open/create the displayed month's note when monthly notes are available, and only falls back to resetting to today when they are not. Returning to today on demand (when monthly notes ARE available) has its own separate, always-present control, covered in US-CAL-02, so the two gestures never compete for the same click.

The vault's real-world indicator is the word-count dot (US-CAL-07); the streak, tags and tasks indicator sources seen in the old plugin are in the icebox (epic ICE) and are intentionally not covered here. AC-CAL-07.4 and AC-CAL-07.5 cover only the two built-in dot sources that ship in this release (note existence and word count); ICE-03 defers the registration surface an external source would need, so no public extension point is promised here.

pn:text-input-suggest-popper-positioning (US-CAL-12) is mapped from a settings text-input autocomplete in the source plugins, but is written here as the generic overlay-positioning behaviour this epic's own hover popover (US-CAL-08) needs; whether it ends up as one shared mechanism with SET's inputs or a duplicated implementation is flagged as an open question rather than assumed.
